answer: No. The class is E33_E41_Linguistic_Appellation, a multiple-instantiation class of E33 Linguistic Object and E41 Appellation used for names in a particular language, which existed only in the RDFS (with even an inconsistent naming, E33_E41 vs E41_E33) and never had a scope note in the base standard. George Bruseker raised this in thread t1649 (Nov 2022, 'error in RDFS for 7.1.1...') and formally opened it as Issue 624 ('Add E33_E41_Linguistic_Appellation to the Official Specification', thread t1655), with Robert Sanderson also supporting adding it. Homework was produced (thread t1682) proposing alternatives (a new P.. property, LRM Nomen, Francesco Beretta's sdh:C11 'Appellation in a Language'), but Martin Doerr and others objected that no adequate scope note/semantics had been agreed (what exactly makes an Appellation 'language-specific', instance-specific vs universal use, etc.). The thread ends in Dec 2022 with Martin still working on a clarifying counter-example and no consensus reached. No later e-vote, decision, or closure of Issue 624 was found anywhere in the archive through Jan 2026 (the latest indexed messages). So the SIG discussed but never agreed to formally add this class with a scope note to CIDOC CRM Base -- it remains RDFS-only and the issue appears to still be open/unresolved.

notes: The archive clearly documents the debate and the formal issue (Issue 624) being opened, but I found no message reporting a final SIG decision (e-vote result, meeting minutes closing the issue, or an approved scope note) for E33_E41_Linguistic_Appellation. Absence of a later resolution in a search-based archive is not airtight proof none exists (e.g. a decision could be recorded in a meeting-minutes document not captured as a mailing-list message), but repeated targeted queries across the full 2022-2026 date range turned up nothing beyond the unresolved Dec 2022 exchange, so I'm treating this as 'never formally agreed' per the archive.
